news_analysis.headline_hook: ₹1.5 Lakh scam! Unga panam epdi waste aaguthu?
news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: A fraudulent eye surgery fundraising campaign on X raised ₹1.5 Lakh from retail donors before sparking widespread controversy and scam allegations.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Retail participants assume that viral traction on social media platforms paired with direct UPI links implies identity verification and legitimate escrow oversight.
news_analysis.institutional_reality: Peer-to-peer social media crowdfunding operates in a regulatory vacuum outside strict SEBI or RBI escrow mandates, turning emotional narrative into zero-recourse capital siphoning.
news_analysis.actionable_retail_rule: Never transfer capital to unverified social media donation links without institutional hospital billing validation or regulated escrow protection.

Social media crowdfunding: Myth vs Reality

comparison_data.myth: Retail belief: Viral post + UPI link = Verified & Safe.
comparison_data.reality: Institutional truth: No SEBI/RBI oversight. It's a regulatory vacuum.

stat_data.label: Total capital siphoned
stat_data.context: Viral posts create a false sense of urgency. Without institutional verification, your Rs 1.5 Lakh contribution isn't an investment; it's a direct loss with zero recourse.

slides.title: How your money vanishes instantly
slides.card_text:
1. Emotional narrative triggers impulsive UPI transfer.
2. Funds bypass escrow/hospital billing verification.
3. Capital is siphoned into untraceable private accounts without any audit trail.

slides.title: Why institutions never donate blindly
slides.card_text: Institutions follow strict due diligence. They verify hospital billing, tax-exempt status (80G), and escrow protection before moving capital. Retail investors often skip this, treating social media as a verified exchange.

slides.title: The Golden Rule: Protect your capital
slides.card_text: Never transfer capital to unverified social media links. Always demand institutional hospital billing validation or regulated escrow proof. If it lacks transparency, treat it as a 100% loss risk.
